purpose: Plan 9 rc compatibility matrix for Star 9

crate_boundary.rule: The reusable rc crate has no dependency on Star 9 runtime, web, CLI, or browser glue.

features.notes: Typed AST covers simple commands, assignments, blocks, parenthesized groups, functions, if/if not across command separators, Plan 9 service-address words such as tcp!host, for/while/switch, pipelines, boolean operators, redirection, process substitution, here documents, and command substitution words.
Supports list assignments, empty lists, positional args, $name, $#name, $"name, subscripts, rc apostrophe quoting, doubled apostrophes, and caret concatenation.
Implements *, ?, character classes, complemented classes, ranges, unmatched literal preservation, and the ~ builtin over host filesystem listings.
Supports sequencing, &&, ||, !, background status, if, for, while, switch, functions, and rc-style status strings including all-zero pipeline success.

Implements <, >, >>, fd-specific output redirects, fd dup/close for captured stdout/stderr, /dev/null handling, stdout/stderr pipe selection, <{} and >{} process substitution through evaluator pipes, and parsed here documents with quoted-delimiter expansion suppression. Pipelines are deterministic in-process evaluator pipelines rather than OS-concurrent process graphs.
Backquote braced command substitution runs through the evaluator and splits output with ifs.

Variables, local command assignments, zero-byte-separated environment export/import, fn#name function export/import, sigexit, and deliver_note(sig*) hooks are implemented in the reusable evaluator. A mounted #env device surface remains an adapter/device integration boundary.

Implements core builtins including ., basename, cd, echo, eval, exec, exit with sigexit, shift, status, test, wait, whatis, ~, true, false, plus host-limited rfork/flag/builtin placeholders. Exact rfork namespace semantics remain host-limited.

External command execution is a host-trait operation. The reusable evaluator searches $path for rc scripts, sets $0/$*, and dispatches wasm/js-looking namespace files back to the host. The Star 9 adapter maps .wasm/.wat through wasi and .js/.mjs through worker while preserving deterministic opt-in host execution behavior.
Native `star9 rc`, `star9 shell --rc`, wasm `createRcShell`, and `<star9-shell rc>` are wired.

The Star 9 adapter can run shell-visible `bind`, `unmount`, `srv`, and `mount` commands through namespace/service files. Loopback services are implemented by default; tcp/network, disk, and vac providers return precise provider-missing errors until corresponding Star 9 providers are configured.
Optional STAR9_RC_ORACLE comparison runs only when configured and compares portable stdout, stderr, and status cases against plan9port or 9front rc.
